# Submission: Aktogay Sulphide Shift Twin

Platform: OpenEgiz v1.0.4.

## Concept

**Enterprise:** The twin represents one sulphide ore value chain at the real
Aktogay open-pit copper operation in Kazakhstan: one representative pit phase,
haulage, a primary crusher, a ROM stockpile and one concentrator line.

**Users:** The primary user is the shift dispatcher, who assigns trucks to
faces and destinations. The shift mining engineer sets blend targets. The
plant shift supervisor needs an estimate of near-term feed rate, grade and
hardness.

**Decision:** After a crusher, truck, haul road or power disruption, how should
the dispatcher reassign trucks and adjust the ore blend to keep concentrator
feed as steady as the available fleet, stockpile and power allow?

**Why this choice:** The crusher and concentrator constrain the linked
production chain. A disruption changes truck cycles and queues, ROM inventory,
feed rate, feed quality, recovery and power demand. Dispatchers need to compare
these effects within a shift. The twin puts those connected states in a
spatial view and exposes repeatable what-if scenarios.

**Real or fictional:** Aktogay is the real site. KAZ Minerals reports the
original sulphide concentrator at 25 Mt/year in *Annual Report and Accounts
2017*, p. 30, and the later second 25 Mt/year concentrator, bringing the
sulphide design capacity to 50 Mt/year. This
submission models one representative 25 Mt/year line, not the whole mine or
plant. The simulation's capacity basis is 3,200 t/h × 24 h/day × 365 day/year
× 90% operating factor = 25.23 Mt/year, rounded to 25 Mt/year. The 90% factor
and 3,200 t/h operating value are modeling assumptions, not a published
Aktogay operating record. Public sources are listed in
`docs/DATA_AND_ASSUMPTIONS.md`.

## Team

**Tau-Ken Labs (Team-064)**. Sole member and developer: **Majhabul Hoque Tahsim**.

| GitHub |
|---|
| **@Catacombs666** |

## Mine

Version 3.0 represents 29 Eclipse Ditto things in namespace `org.aktogay`: the
mine, three areas, one pit phase, three ore faces, one waste cut, two haul roads,
two shared shovels, eight truck twins (2–8 active), a crusher, ROM stockpile,
concentrator, substation, maintenance crew, dispatch service, waste dump and tailings accounting twin. `_parents`
represents containment; `feeds`, `supplies`, `connects` and `loaded_by` record
process relationships. Three-dimensional scene positions are illustrative.

The mine is a seeded, bounded-step material-flow model. Shovel loading resources
and the ROM dump bay serialize service; vehicles carry sampled copper/hardness
through their full cycles. ROM capacity, crusher capacity, hardness and available
power constrain downstream flow. Ore, waste and contained-copper balances are
checked. The line design basis is not a guarantee of achieved shift production.

## Modules and What-if Scenarios

| Module | Working behavior | Where to inspect |
|---|---|---|
| Haulage and dispatch | Loading queues, loaded/empty travel, dump queue, fleet availability; adaptive face selection considers grade, hardness and shovel queue. Fixed rotation is a selectable comparison policy. | 3D trucks, asset inspector, dispatcher log, Settings |
| ROM, crushing and plant | Finite ROM, mass-weighted mixing, actual processed tonnes, hardness derate, power cap and synthetic recovery. | KPI strip, ROM pile, feed chart, crusher/plant/substation inspection |
| Paired decision experiment | Two 60-minute forecasts from the identical current material and random state: baseline versus chosen fault. Result passes through the platform. | Look one hour ahead; exportable confirmed report |

Start the run using **Start Simulation**. In **What-if laboratory**, choose a
card and press **Run selected scenario**. Changing the card alone changes no
operating state. All scenarios can be undone using **Restore normal conditions**;
**Reset** clears the shift counters and returns READY using the current settings.

| Scenario | Model consequence | What is visible |
|---|---|---|
| Crusher outage | Crusher throughput stops; arrivals fill ROM until trucks queue. ROM cannot feed past the stopped crusher. | Fault indication, zero feed, changing inventory, queue and event |
| Truck breakdown | HT-03 (or the first active truck in a two-truck fleet) stops in place; its payload remains accounted for. | Stationary failed asset, reduced active fleet, retained payload |
| Main road closure | Committed trucks clear the route; subsequent trips use the longer north route with distance and gradient dependent travel. | Closure barrier, changed truck routes, longer cycles |
| Power curtailment | Supply is capped at 45 MW or the configured lower supply. | Substation state; feed ≤ 45,000/21 = 2,143 t/h |
| Low-grade F2 | New loads sample 0.18% Cu. Existing loads retain their quality. | Face condition, dispatch choices and delayed mixed feed change |
| Shovel outage | SH-02 stops. Partial payload is held. Future assignments use available shovels. | Fault state, queues, new assignments and delayed feed effects |
| Road congestion | Main road admission falls to 12 vehicles/hour/direction. | Entry queues, road overlay and wait counters |
| Hard F3 | New F3 loads sample 20 kWh/t. Adaptive dispatch can avoid F3. | Face condition, changed assignments; delayed or small plant response |

## Version 3 engineering additions

Finite ore reserves decrease during loading and depleted faces stop supplying
material. Roads admit trucks at a bounded headway per direction. Distance,
gradient and loaded/empty state determine travel time. Bucket size determines
loading passes. Waste and processing tailings have explicit accounting twins.
The resource overlay shows reserves, queues and faults. Scenario propagation
panels distinguish observed changes from matched forecasts.

The dispatch comparison runs fixed rotation and adaptive dispatch from the same
paused state and matched per-truck loading variation. It reports production,
grade error, waiting, energy and final ROM. The live shift remains unchanged.
An infeasible blend target generates a warning. See `docs/V3_UPGRADE.md`.

## Mine visualization

**http://localhost:8091** provides a locally bundled Three.js scene: graded pit
benches and ramp, moving articulated haul trucks, shared excavators, crusher,
ROM, conveyors, concentrator and substation. Orbit/pan/zoom, Fit/Top view and asset
inspection support exploration. Trucks follow confirmed route progress; loading,
dumping, breakdown, road closure and plant status are reflected visually.

The UI does not combine initial twin values with newer local events. The entire
operator snapshot is published through MQTT and read back from one Ditto feature,
with a run ID, sequence and timestamp. Stale state holds the scene and is labelled.
The separate local development mode is explicitly labelled and is not the Stand.

## Data and Assumptions

The published Aktogay identity, process route and line capacity remain the only
real-site grounding. Every operating grade, cycle, fleet setting, inventory,
recovery response and coordinate is synthetic. See `docs/DATA_AND_ASSUMPTIONS.md`
for sources, equations and ranges; `ASSET_CREDITS.md` for third-party graphics rights.
Settings apply to a new paused/ready shift, so changes do not erase in-flight
material during normal operation. The model is not calibrated to operator records.

## What works and what does not

Version 3 model/API validation passes 31 tests. A five-seed, five-condition
benchmark records all 25 matched policy comparisons, including adverse tradeoffs.
The v3 browser interface is implemented but has not been visually verified here.
User-supplied screenshots in the presentation show the preceding working version.
They are labelled accordingly and do not prove v3 integration.

**Not yet verified:** Docker/Stand startup, real broker delivery and Ditto
acceptance, Telegraf/InfluxDB ingestion and Grafana display. Docker is absent in
the authoring environment. Run `bash scripts/verify-aktogay.sh` after the integrated
startup; it checks these paths and writes an honest pass/fail report. A broker
publish alone is never treated as confirmation of a twin update.

## Limitations

The model has shared shovel resources, but no shovel relocation time, detailed
truck collision/overtaking dynamics, surveyed terrain, calibrated comminution circuit, fuel consumption, automatic repair duration,
tailings storage engineering or operational safety logic. Road lengths and 3D scene units
are different scales; equipment is enlarged for readability. Graphics quality
is selectable and software rendering has a reduced-resolution profile. All
state is in memory and a service restart begins a new shift; reports can be exported.

## Presentation

`presentation.pdf` describes the concept, 3D controls, platform data path,
scenario behavior, paired experiment, data assumptions and verification boundary.

     2	
     3	An interactive 3D digital twin of one representative Aktogay sulphide line:
     4	pit faces → haulage → ROM → primary crusher → concentrator feed.
     5	Operating inputs and terrain are synthetic. Site identity and the approximately
     6	25 Mt/year line basis are grounded in the sources in
     7	[Data and Assumptions](docs/DATA_AND_ASSUMPTIONS.md).

     9	## Version 3
    10	
    11	Finite reserves, road admission queues, gradient-dependent travel, bucket-based
    12	loading, two additional scenarios, resource overlays and matched dispatch
    13	experiments strengthen the original model. Read [the upgrade guide](docs/V3_UPGRADE.md)
    14	for the exact changes and a judge demonstration sequence.
    15

    17	Docker integration still require the checks below on your machine. Historical
    18	screenshots show the preceding version, not an independently verified v3 run.
    19	
    20	## Start the OpenEgiz submission
    21	
    22	Requirements: Docker Engine/Desktop running, Docker Compose v2.20+, Python 3,
    23	`make`, and at least 6 GiB available to Docker. First startup downloads platform
    24	images and one pinned Python dependency. No account, API key or paid service is
    25	needed. All browser graphics dependencies and textures are bundled locally.
    26	
    27	On Ubuntu, install the missing command-line prerequisite:
    28	
    29	```bash
    30	sudo apt-get update
    31	sudo apt-get install -y make
    32	```
    33	
    34	From the repository root (the directory containing this README and Makefile):
    35	
    36	```bash
    37	make aktogay
    38	```
    39	
    40	Open **http://localhost:8091**, then click **Start Simulation**. Startup leaves
    41	the model READY so the beginning of the shift is visible. When running, trucks
    42	complete loading, haul, dump and return cycles, the simulated clock advances,
    43	and the KPI/chart values update. The header must show **DITTO CONFIRMED** for an
    44	integrated run. It does not label missing or stale state as live.
    45	
    46	Grafana: **http://localhost:3000** → Dashboards → OpenEgiz Examples →
    47	**Aktogay Sulphide Shift Twin**. Login is `admin` with the generated
    48	`GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `deploy/compose/.env`. Keep that file private.
    49	
    50	### Updating an existing local installation
    51	
    52	Copy the updated source files into your existing project folder, preserving
    53	`deploy/compose/.env` and Docker volumes. Then run `make aktogay` again; it
    54	rebuilds the image with the new model and locally bundled 3D files. Reload the
    55	browser with Ctrl+Shift+R. No `make clean` is required.
    56	
    57	On the team's Windows/WSL installation:
    58	
    59	```bash
    60	cd /mnt/e/team-064-main
    61	make aktogay
    62	```
    63	
    64	Run these commands in Ubuntu, with Ubuntu enabled in Docker Desktop → Settings
    65	→ Resources → WSL Integration. A Windows drive E: appears as `/mnt/e/` in WSL.
    66	
    67	## Operator workflow
    68	
    69	1. **Start Simulation**. The default clock is 60×, or one simulated minute per
    70	   real second. Choose 1×, 10×, 30×, 60×, 120× or 180× using Time scale.
    71	2. Drag the scene to orbit; right-drag to pan; scroll to zoom. Fit view and Top
    72	   restore useful camera positions. Click equipment or an asset label to inspect
    73	   its current state. Geometry is schematic and equipment is enlarged for clarity.
    74	3. Open **What-if laboratory**, select a disruption, and click **Run selected
    75	   scenario** while running. Merely selecting a card does not change the mine.
    76	   The active condition appears beneath the controls and in the dispatcher log.
    77	4. **Restore normal conditions** clears the fault without discarding material
    78	   already mined or processed. **Reset** creates a new READY shift with the
    79	   current settings and an 8,000 t ROM; it does not delete Docker data.
    80	5. **Pause Simulation**, then open **Settings**. Apply & reset shift validates
    81	   inputs and starts a new READY shift. Settings cannot silently alter an ongoing
    82	   material inventory. Time scale alone can be changed while running.
    83	6. **Compare next 60 min** performs two seeded forecasts from the same current
    84	   inventory/RNG state: normal conditions versus the selected disruption. It
    85	   does not advance the operating run. This result also returns through Ditto.
    86	7. **Export run** downloads the confirmed snapshot, assumptions/settings,
    87	   recent history, event log and paired forecast as JSON.
    88	
    89	The ROM is upstream of the crusher. It stores incoming ore during a crusher
    90	outage; it cannot bypass the stopped crusher to keep the plant fed. Grade and
    91	hardness changes affect newly sampled loads, then travel through haulage and
    92	ROM blending. Consequently not every scenario causes an instantaneous feed
    93	change. The hard-F3 scenario may have little feed effect when adaptive dispatch
    94	avoids that face; the changed face twin and later assignments remain visible.
    95

    97	
    98	Model and HTTP API tests (standard Python library only):
    99	
   100	```bash
   101	make test-aktogay
   102	```
   103	
   104	After the real Docker stack is running, verify MQTT → Ditto, confirmed state,
   105	all scenarios, balances, pause/reset, InfluxDB and Grafana:
   106	
   107	```bash
   108	bash scripts/verify-aktogay.sh
   109	```
   110	
   111	This exercises and resets the in-memory simulation. It writes
   112	`docs/evidence/stand-report.json`; a failing check returns a nonzero exit code.
   113	Optional browser test instructions are in [Validation](docs/VALIDATION_REPORT.md).
   114	
   115	**Verification boundary:** the bundled model/API and browser reports were
   116	produced with the same simulation/service in explicitly labelled local mode.
   117	Docker is unavailable in the authoring environment. Integrated startup, Ditto
   118	acceptance, Grafana ingestion and clean-machine startup duration still require
   119	the above Stand check. They are not claimed as passed.
   120	
   121	## Lightweight local preview (not an OpenEgiz Stand)
   122	
   123	To inspect the 3D interface and exercise the same model without Docker:
   124	
   125	```bash
   126	make aktogay-local
   127	```
   128	
   129	Open http://localhost:8091. The header states **LOCAL MODEL · PLATFORM OFF**.
   130	This mode does not connect to MQTT, Ditto or Grafana and is not the contest
   131	execution path. Do not run it on the same port as the integrated service.
   132	
   133	## Stop, status and troubleshooting
   134	
   135	```bash
   136	make ps
   137	make logs S=aktogay-mine
   138	make down
   139	```
   140	
   141	`make down` preserves platform volumes; restarting the simulator creates a new
   142	in-memory shift. Export a report before stopping if it is needed. `make clean`
   143	deletes platform volumes and credentials and is not needed for this update.
   144	
   145	| Symptom | Action |
   146	|---|---|
   147	| Start disabled / WAITING FOR DITTO | Inspect `make logs S=aktogay-mine` and `make logs S=ditto-connectivity`; the overlay requires a confirmed `operator_state` feature, not just an MQTT connection. |
   148	| Old 2D interface | Rebuild with `make aktogay`, then hard-refresh the browser. |
   149	| SIM clock/events/KPIs disagree | The model uses one atomic platform snapshot. Verify the image was rebuilt and that the new API returns `snapshot` and `transport`. |
   150	| Slow graphics | Use the efficient/default quality and a smaller window. Software renderers are detected automatically. High quality increases pixel density and requires more rendering capacity. |
   151	| 3D unavailable | Enable browser hardware acceleration/WebGL. A graphics error is reported; no static image is passed off as 3D. |
   152	| Docker unavailable in Ubuntu | Enable Ubuntu WSL integration and check that `docker version` lists both Client and Server. |
   153	
   154	## Important files
   155	
   156	- `team/aktogay/model.py`: seeded queues, haul cycles, balances, blending and energy limits.
   157	- `team/aktogay/app.py`: controls, MQTT protocol, atomic Ditto readback and HTTP/static server.
   158	- `team/aktogay/static/scene.js`: original procedural 3D scene and state-driven equipment.
   159	- `team/aktogay/static/ui.js`, `style.css`: controls, charts, settings and inspection.
   160	- `team/aktogay/setup_twins.py`: 29 twins, containment and process relations.

1	# Data and assumptions
     2	
     3	## Public site facts
     4	
     5	The twin uses Aktogay as a real-world reference for the site identity and
     6	process route. KAZ Minerals describes Aktogay as an open-pit operation in
     7	Kazakhstan with two sulphide concentrators and a combined design capacity of
     8	50 Mt/year. Its public materials describe the original concentrator at 25
     9	Mt/year and the second 25 Mt/year expansion.
    10	
    11	Sources:
    12	
    13	1. KAZ Minerals, [Annual Report and Accounts 2017](https://www.kazminerals.com/media/6188/kaz-minerals-2017-ara-web-ready-version.pdf),
    14	   p. 30, Aktogay section. Reports 25 million tonnes per year capacity for the
    15	   existing concentrator when fully ramped up and the expansion plan to double
    16	   sulphide processing capacity to 50 million tonnes per year.
    17	2. KAZ Minerals, [Aktogay](https://www.kazminerals.com/our-locations/aktogay/),
    18	   official operations page, accessed 15 October 2026. Reports two sulphide
    19	   concentrators with combined capacity of 50 Mtpa.
    20	3. KAZ Minerals, [Aktogay expansion project approved](https://www.kazminerals.com/aktogay-expansion-project-approved/),
    21	   2017. States that the first sulphide concentrator had 25 Mt/year capacity
    22	   and the expansion would double it to 50 Mt/year.
    23	4. KAZ Minerals, [Presidential opening of the Aktogay expansion project](https://www.kazminerals.com/presidential-opening-of-the-aktogay-expansion-project/),
    24	   2021. Describes the new 25 Mtpa concentrator and the resulting 50 Mtpa
    25	   combined sulphide capacity.
    26	
    27	The model chooses one representative 25 Mt/year line. It does not represent
    28	the site's two-line combined capacity as one line. The annualized simulator
    29	basis is:
    30	
    31	`3,200 t/h × 24 h/day × 365 day/year × 0.90 availability = 25.23 Mt/year`
    32	
    33	The 3,200 t/h and 90% factor are synthetic model settings selected to express
    34	one 25 Mt/year line. They are not statements of actual Aktogay operating
    35	throughput or availability.
    36	
    37	## Synthetic values and adjustable ranges
    38	
    39	| Parameter | Default | UI range / rule |
    40	|---|---:|---|
    41	| Active 220 t trucks | 8 | 2–8; remaining twins are parked |
    42	| Shovel loading | 6.5 min | 3–12 min, seeded ±8% variability; two shared resources |
    43	| Main loaded haul | 9 min | 5–20 min; reference speed at 6% main-road grade |
    44	| Empty return | 0.85 × loaded-leg duration | Longer alternative route remains effective |
    45	| Main/north road distance | 3.8 / 5.2 km | Used in travel time; scene units are schematic |
    46	| Ore-face grades F1/F2/F3 | 0.31 / 0.39 / 0.27 % Cu | Each 0.10–1.00 % Cu |
    47	| Grade target | 0.34 % Cu | 0.15–0.80 % Cu; target may be infeasible for selected face grades |
    48	| Base hardness | 12.4 kWh/t | 8–24; face offsets +0.6 / −0.9 / +2.6 |
    49	| ROM capacity / initial inventory | 24,000 / 8,000 t | Initial grade 0.34%; hardness equals configured base |
    50	| Crusher capacity | 3,200 t/h | 500–4,500 t/h |
    51	| Specific combined plant energy | 21 kWh/t | Fixed illustrative intensity; 8 crusher + 13 concentrator |
    52	| Available power | 75 MW | 10–90 MW; fault caps supply at min(configured,45) |
    53	| Simulation speed | 60× | 1–180× |
    54	| Seed | 64 | Integer 0–999999 |
    55	
    56	One waste assignment occurs per eleven dispatches. SH-02 serves F2; SH-01 is a
    57	shared loading resource for F1/F3/waste. Shovel relocation time is omitted.
    58	The ROM dumping bay handles one truck at a time, with a 72-second service.
    59	Grades and hardness are sampled at the start of loading and remain attached to
    60	that material. New settings require pause and reset; speed alone changes live.
    61	All of these are modeling assumptions, not disclosed Aktogay operating data.
    62	
    63	## Accounting and response equations
    64	
    65	- Ore residual: `initial_ROM + ore_mined − processed − current_ROM − ore_on_trucks`.
    66	- Waste residual: `waste_mined − waste_dumped − waste_on_trucks`.
    67	- Copper residual: `initial_ROM_Cu + mined_Cu − processed_Cu − ROM_Cu − truck_Cu`.
    68	- All copper accounting uses **tonnes of contained copper**: `tonnes × grade_pct / 100`.
    69	- ROM quality is mass-weighted. Processing removes ore, copper and hardness mass
    70	  in the same proportion. Concentrate mass is `processed_Cu × recovery / 0.25`,
    71	  assuming 25% Cu concentrate. That concentrate grade is synthetic too.
    72	- Feed capacity is `min(crusher_tph × hardness_factor, available_MW × 1000 / 21)`.
    73	- `hardness_factor = max(0.52, 1 − max(0, hardness−12) × 0.045)`.
    74	- Actual processed tonnes are bounded by available ROM in each timestep. The
    75	  displayed feed is the measured equivalent rate for the latest integration step.
    76	- Recovery is bounded between 62% and 94% with a simple hardness penalty and
    77	  grade adjustment; it is a teaching approximation, not a plant-performance curve.
    78	
    79	The annual 90% operating factor above is used only for the design-capacity basis.
    80	It is not applied again as a constant 10% derate at every processing step.
    81	
    82	## Scenarios, prediction and geometry
    83	
    84	Crusher downtime stops downstream feed because ROM is upstream. Existing
    85	truck payloads are conserved during breakdown. Trucks committed to the main
    86	road clear it; new trips use the north route, avoiding an instantaneous spatial
    87	teleport. Low-grade and hard-ore changes apply to future samples; no fictitious
    88	4 kt parcel is injected into ROM to force a response.
    89	
    90	The paired experiment clones inventory, truck states and RNG, restores normal
    91	conditions for one copy and applies the selected fault to the other, then
    92	integrates both for 60 minutes. It is a conditional model experiment, not an
    93	operating forecast calibrated to the real mine. Clearing a condition does not
    94	remove material already mined under that condition.
    95	
    96	3D coordinates are scene units, not surveyed metres. Truck and shovel size is
    97	exaggerated for legibility. The renderer interpolates only between received
    98	states; the backend controls all simulated progress. Road admission uses per-direction headway. Collisions, overtaking, road curvature and shovel relocation are not modeled.
    99	
   100	## Data rights
   101	
   102	No mine datasets are redistributed. Public sources above are retained by link.
   103	All operating inputs are original synthetic examples. Third-party graphics and
   104	software are attributed in `ASSET_CREDITS.md`, under their original licenses.
   105	
   106	## Version 3 constraints and assumptions
   107	
   108	All new parameters below are synthetic, not Aktogay measurements.
   109	
   110	- Ore reserves: 85,000 t per face, adjustable 220–150,000 t. Waste cut: 120,000 t.
   111	  Loading deducts reserves continuously; final loads may be partial. Restore
   112	  normal conditions does not replenish a depleted face. Reset starts a new shift.
   113	- Road admission: 36 vehicles/h per direction by default, adjustable 6–60.
   114	  Minimum headway = 3,600 / capacity seconds. Congestion caps main-road capacity
   115	  at 12. Trucks initially on roads are a seeded initial condition.
   116	- Main/north grade: 6% / 8%, adjustable 0–12%. Reference flat speed =
   117	  (3.8 km / reference haul hours) × 1.30. Loaded speed divides this by
   118	  (1 + 0.05 × grade); empty speed additionally divides by 0.85. Speeds cap
   119	  at 45 km/h loaded and 50 km/h empty. Travel time = distance / speed.
   120	  These coefficients approximate the direction of response, not vehicle physics.
   121	- Bucket: 45 t nominal, adjustable 25–65, fill factor 0.90.
   122	  Passes = ceil(target payload / (bucket × 0.90)). Service time = passes ×
   123	  reference loading minutes / 6 × seeded variation (0.92–1.08).
   124	- Tailings mass = processed ore − concentrate. Tailings contained copper =
   125	  processed contained copper − recovered copper. No water/geotechnical model.
   126	- Dispatch grade error is mass-weighted absolute deviation from target in
   127	  percentage points. Fleet waiting minutes sum waits across all trucks.
   128	- Resource and processing residuals supplement the ore/waste/copper balances.
   129	
   130	Mechanism reference: Caterpillar, “Ensure Your Haul Roads Are an Asset”
   131	https://www.cat.com/en_US/blog/mining/articles/ensure-haul-roads-are-an-asset.html
   132	explains why grade and road condition matter. It does not supply our coefficients.
   133	
   134	A policy experiment deep-copies the same current state into both alternatives,
   135	changes only dispatch policy, and applies the same scenario and horizon.
   136	Per-truck loading variation uses seed, truck ID and load count. Already committed
   137	loads retain assignments. Results are conditional simulation evidence. In low-grade
   138	conditions, higher production can come with worse grade error. Final ROM is shown
   139	because higher throughput may consume an existing buffer rather than improve supply.
